html:
SMTO-CFG-0041 — SMTO's model context size setting is zero or negative

GUID: ae757727-926e-4ffb-b3ee-4fbf5f51e37e
Slug: config-llm-context-window-tokens-must-be-greater
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting tells SMTO how much text the AI model can consider at once (its context size), but it is set to zero or a negative number, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find context_window_tokens under the llm section. That line sets the model's context size.
  2. Change it to your model's context size (a whole number of tokens, such as 32768), or delete the line so SMTO uses the size measured from the model server. Then start SMTO again. A context size of zero or less can't hold any text; leaving it out lets SMTO measure it automatically.
  3. If SMTO is started by a script or service, ask its owner to check the AOR_LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS setting too; it must be empty or above zero. That setting overrides the file, so a zero there causes the same stop.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits or timeouts to work around this; only the context size is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Configuration validation failed because an explicit llm.context_window_tokens value (or AOR_LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS) is zero or negative.

What this means

  • An explicit context_window_tokens value is zero or negative; an omitted value follows normal configuration resolution. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • An explicit context_window_tokens value is zero or negative; an omitted value follows normal configuration resolution.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the explicit token-window value against the model's actual supported context, not the output-token limit.

How to fix it

  • Set llm.context_window_tokens in the bootstrap YAML to a positive integer the model supports, or omit it (null) to use the server's measured capacity. Also check AOR_LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS, which overrides the file and is validated by Settings, then restart the Server.
  • Supply the model's supported positive context-window size or use its normal resolved default.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported positive context window is captured for the intended task.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
